Love the witcher series? Hate it when the edges of your screen are blurry? well the witcher 3 lets you turn off chromatic abberation.

I understand some people and companies wanting to duplicate the limits and flaws of the human eye and the camera lens, with shit like lens flare, depth of field and this chromatic abberation, but I can't stand it and these are the first options I look for to disable when starting up a new game.

Many of these features exist because someone who is really into graphics programming and physics thought to themselves "Huh, I bet I could do that in a game" while watching a film or making photos etc. Proud of their work, they show their collegues the ten lines of fragment shader code that look like magic until they explain and then rightfully earn earn applause and marvel. And then someone sais "Let's put this in the game and impress everyone with a trailer". And none of this is bad until it becomes an "industry standard" because "we need to keep up with the features of those guys".

Source: Been there, seen that happen (not in the games industry though, but very close to it).
